newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims fell in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, April 5 Continued Claims from 2,316,000 and March 29 from 2,298,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 328,000 in the April 19 week.
The four-week moving average for the week ended April 19 was the highest since February 8, when it reached 325,500.
Labor said 10 states and one territory reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended April 12, the latest period for which data are available.
Among the largest were Michigan, with 4,200; Puerto Rico, 2,767; North Carolina, 2,746; Alabama, with 2,566; Washington, with 2,055; and Pennsylvania, 2,002.

Michigan reported layoffs in the automobile industry, while Puerto Rico said it had layoffs in the apparel, leather goods and petroleum industries. North Carolina reported layoffs in the textile, furniture and transportation equipment industries.

Alabama had layoffs in the textile, apparel, trade and service industries. Pennsylvania attributed the increase to layoffs in the fabricated metals and service industries. Washington provided no reason for the increase in claims.
Six states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 in the April 12 week.
They were California, with 3,275; New Jersey, 2,547; Oregon, with 1,948; Illinois, with 1,750; Massachusetts, with 1,558; and Arkansas, with 1,080.

California and Oregon gave no reason for the drop in claims. New Jersey said it had fewer layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries. Illinois reported fewer layoffs in the trade and service industries and manufacturing.
Arkansas said it had fewer layoffs in the electrical equipment industries.
